reasoning: Polling in the last 45 days for Florida’s 2026 U.S. Senate race consistently shows Republican Sen. Ashley Moody leading Democratic challengers Angie Nixon and Alex Vindman by **8–10 points**, indicating an **R+8–10** environment in current head‑to‑head general‑election polling.[1][2][3][6][8][9][11] Decision Desk HQ’s statewide polling average also has Moody ahead of Vindman by **7 points (47–40)**, reinforcing a GOP advantage in the race.[11][13] There is no recent, state‑specific 2026 presidential general‑election polling for Florida in the gathered results, so the clearest current margin is for the Senate contest, with Republicans holding a high single‑digit to low double‑digit lead that is broadly consistent with Florida’s structural R+5 Cook PVI.[7]

sources.name: Florida Phoenix (UNF PORL poll)
sources.details: University of North Florida Public Opinion Research Lab poll of 848 likely midterm voters finds Sen. Ashley Moody leading Angie Nixon 50–42 (R+8) and Alex Vindman 50–40 (R+10) in Florida’s 2026 Senate general-election matchups.

sources.name: Tallahassee Democrat (UNF PORL poll)
sources.details: Tallahassee Democrat report on the same UNF PORL survey notes Moody at 50% versus Nixon at 42% (R+8) and Vindman at 40% (R+10), describing the statewide Senate and governor contests as notably closer than previous cycles but still with Moody ahead.

sources.name: Politico (summary of UNF PORL poll)
sources.details: Politico’s Florida Playbook summarizes the UNF PORL poll, stating Moody has a 10‑point lead over Vindman and an 8‑point lead over Nixon in the Florida Senate race, both within the poll’s ±3.8% margin of error but showing her in a strong position.

sources.name: Florida Politics / Sunburn (UNF PORL recap)
sources.details: Florida Politics’ Sunburn newsletter recaps the UNF PORL survey, noting Ashley Moody leads Alex Vindman by 10 points and Angie Nixon by 8 points in hypothetical November Senate matchups.

sources.name: Courthouse News (UNF PORL poll coverage)
sources.details: Courthouse News, reporting on Democratic efforts to unseat Moody, cites the UNF PORL July poll showing Moody at 50% against Nixon (42%) and Vindman (40%), underscoring the GOP incumbent’s sizable lead.

sources.name: Decision Desk HQ Florida Senate polling average
sources.details: Decision Desk HQ’s Florida 2026 Senate polling average shows Ashley Moody leading Alex Vindman 47–40 (R+7) and characterizes Florida as likely to remain in Republican hands with roughly a 4‑in‑5 GOP win probability.
sources.date_range: Not specified (Decision Desk HQ polling average current as of August 9, 2026)

sources.name: Florida Politics / Sunburn (UNF PORL governor matchup)
sources.details: UNF PORL’s same July poll finds Byron Donalds leading Democrat David Jolly 46–41 (R+5) in the 2026 Florida gubernatorial race, providing contextual evidence that statewide GOP margins are high single digits but this is not a Senate or presidential contest.

sources.name: El País (UNF PORL governor matchup coverage)
sources.details: El País notes that in the UNF PORL July poll, Donalds leads Jolly 46–41 (R+5) among likely November voters in the race to succeed DeSantis, highlighting a narrower but still Republican-leaning statewide environment compared to recent cycles; this is gubernatorial, not Senate or presidential data.

sources.name: Cook Political Report – Cook Partisan Voting Index (Florida statewide)
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s statewide Partisan Voting Index table lists Florida as R+5, indicating the state voted about five points more Republican than the national average in the most recent presidential election; this is a structural measure, not 2026 polling.
sources.date_range: State PVI based on last completed presidential election (data current through 2024 cycle)
